title.narrative: RanMarine Durban Port Pilot, South Africa

description.narrative: Durban is the largest and busiest shipping terminal in sub-Saharan Africa – handling more than 30 million tonnes of cargo per year – and the fourth largest container terminal in the southern hemisphere. Three large rivers flow into the Durban port area bringing a constant stream of floating debris. Flooding also occurs regularly, three to four times a year, which brings a dramatic increase of debris. Regular removal of debris and other waste is necessary to keep this port operational. Unfortunately, waste removal not only requires closure of commercial spaces, it also causes costly damage to equipment and vessels moored in the Port, which is a real economic concern for Durban and any port alike.RanMarine Technology B.V. is a Dutch environmental technology company that develops Unmanned Autonomous Vessels (UAVs), also known as aquatic drones or Sharks, to collect waste in waters with the aim to reduce and prevent waste and plastics from ending up in the world’s oceans. RanMarine’s Sharks can provide a continuous, non-stop, 24/7 waste removal service in a manner that is cleaner, less toxic, faster and considerably cost-effective for ports compared to commonly used removal services and this may offer a suitable solution for the issues Durban and other ports in South Africa are facing. To prepare for future investments in South Africa, Technical Assistance (DGGF) provided support to validate RanMarine’s technology in South African ports.The project included partner selection in Durban and Cape Town, a pilot with 2 drones (Waste Sharks) and a docking station in local waters to test and improve waste collection and recycle value. The project also contributed to the upskilling and knowledge transfer of local workforce by training 10 drone operators and waste managers.Based on the validation results, further investments and product development to meet local market demand are currently being explored; in 2018 and 2019 RanMarine continued to engaged with government entries in South Africa and are now looking to export product to South Africa as of 2020.
